glance_takeaway: The page is a bioacoustics ML project ('murmur') framed as a mountain-climbing expedition 'up the macro-F1 slope.' A non-expert would understand it is about teaching a small audio classifier to recognize birds using cheap, physically-plausible (reverb) noise augmentations instead of reaching for a bigger model. The main message: the bet 'partially works' — the augmentation route climbed +5.9 points (0.612 at Trailhead to 0.671 at High Camp), but the 'summit' (rare-species ceiling) is still in cloud. The line chart shows waypoints: Trailhead (no aug, 0.612), Camp 2 (light reverb, 0.641), a Ravine 'turned back' failure (pitch/stretch, 0.589), Camp 4 (+noise mix, 0.643), High Camp (the stack, 0.671, best), and a Summit-in-cloud with a rare-tail concern ('is 41 clips even learnable?'), plus heavy reverb at 0.663.

F1.note: Header 'The wager' states both halves: cheap reverb-inspired augs improve small-data bird classification AND beat spending same compute on a bigger/pretrained backbone; verdict revisits the efficiency (H2) claim.

F2.note: '6,200 clips, 34 species' in wager; 'log-mel, 128 mels' in recipe table. Clip duration (5 s), mono, and 32 kHz sample rate are not stated, but the dataset-size meaning lands.

F3.note: 70/15/15 stratified/seeded split and ~930 val size not stated. Only the ~930-clip test split is mentioned (footer: 'the ~930-clip test split has not been touched during search'); the split design itself is absent.

F4.note: Long-tail emphasized throughout; per-species table shows top class American Robin at 480 clips and deep-tail Kirtland's Warbler at 41, with common/mid/rare/deep-tail tiers. Detailed distribution stats (11 <80, 5 <45, median ~120, 8 classes ~52%) are not on the page.

F5.note: Legend: 'Height on the map = validation macro-F1 ... weights the rare tail equally with the common head.' One-glance section: seed wobble '~ +/-0.006.'

F6.note: Ledger row 01 baseline-clean 2026-03-08 = 0.612 'floor'; Trailhead section 'Establishes where the climb starts: 0.612 ... no augmentation.'

F7.note: Camp 2 section: light IR reverb RT60 0.3-0.6 s, p=0.5, 0.641 (+0.029), 'first clear win.' Ledger row 02 matches.

F8.note: The ravine section: pitch +/-2 semitones + time-stretch 0.9-1.1x on top of Camp 2, 0.589, 'below the no-aug baseline.' Ledger row 03 = 0.589 regression.

F9.note: Camp 4 section: SNR-controlled noise mixing 5-20 dB, 0.643, '+0.002 over Camp 2, inside run-to-run noise. A null result.' Ledger note confirms +0.002 vs exp-02.

F10.note: High Camp section + ledger row 05: full stack (light reverb + noise mix + SpecAugment + partial class-balanced sampler), 0.671, +0.059, 'best.'

F11.note: The spur section + ledger row 06: heavy long-RT60 (0.8-1.5 s), p=0.7, 0.663, below best; 'Common up, rare down, small net loss.'

F12.note: Ravine section: 'Warping pitch and tempo smears the fine formant and timing cues the rare classes depend on ... Common classes shrug it off, hiding the asymmetric harm.' The '<50 real clips to anchor' detail is not explicit but mechanism conveyed.

F13.note: Camp 4 + ledger note: +0.002 inside +/-0.006 seed noise, read as null; 'Kept in the pack anyway on the hunch that it would compose with SpecAugment further up.'

F14.note: 'The recipe at High Camp' table lists small_cnn, log-mel-128, class_balanced 0.5, reverb p0.5 RT60 0.3-0.6, noise_mix 5-20 dB, specaugment 2 freq/2 time, and OFF row for pitch/stretch + heavy reverb. Exact match.

F15.note: Per-species table matches exactly: Robin 0.79->0.85, Cardinal 0.76->0.83, Song Sparrow 0.68->0.74, Wood Thrush 0.51->0.54, Kirtland's 0.34->0.33 (-0.01); '~4.5 of those 5.9 points come from the common and mid tiers.'

render_issues: Minor label crowding at the summit region of the SVG: the gold '0.671 - best' text sits close to the 'High Camp / the stack' and 'Summit - in cloud' cloud labels and the dashed planned-route lines cross that area; still legible in full.png. In the glance viewport the right-edge 'heavy reverb - 0.663' label is slightly clipped. Nothing broken.
strengths: Exceptionally faithful: 14 of 15 facts conveyed with exact numbers, including the full ledger, per-species decomposition, and best-config table.

Glance is highly effective — the headline states the verdict verbatim ('partially works ... +5.9 points ... summit still in cloud') and the chart shows the regression (Ravine) and the best-vs-heavy-reverb result.

Outstanding caveat fidelity: seed noise, null result, per-tier-not-per-class caveats, H2-not-shown, a dedicated 'Where this map lies' honesty section, and the untouched test split are all surfaced. No overselling.

Honest, purposeful visual encoding: height = macro-F1 with a real axis, waypoints at true scores, dashed spurs for abandoned runs, clouds for the unknown ceiling; the legend explicitly disclaims decorative ridges as carrying no meaning.
weaknesses: Split design (70/15/15, stratified, seeded, ~930 val) is essentially absent; only the test split size is mentioned.
Some F2/F4 sub-details missing (5 s / mono / 32 kHz clip format; distribution stats like median ~120 and 8-classes-52%), though the meaning-bearing facts land.
Long single-scroll page with no table of contents or anchors; the metaphor names (Ravine, spur, High Camp) require mapping back to exp numbers, though the exp tags help.
Label crowding at the most important data point (0.671 best) in the SVG summit area slightly hurts legibility.
Next-steps (T4, class-conditional augmentation) do not surface at all in the glance.
evaluator_notes: A genuinely excellent, harsh-standard-clearing page. Accuracy is formulaically high (14/15 conveyed, 1 absent, no distortions or contradictions = 9.3) and warranted by a near-complete, faithful rendering. Glance scored 7.5: topic plus T1 (partial support, +5.9) and T2 (pitch/stretch regression) land clearly, T3 (stack is best; heavy reverb below) mostly lands, T4 (next steps) is absent above the fold. Depth is strong (8.0) given the thorough per-experiment mechanisms, per-species table, open-questions, and verdict; density is appropriate for the technical-collaborator audience though the page runs long. Overall = 0.35*9.3 + 0.30*7.5 + 0.15*8.0 + 0.10*7.5 + 0.10*7.5 = 8.2.
